title: From the cell to the king's inner circle.
subtitle: One conversation, and trust was won
then: Once Yusuf's innocence was clear, the king wanted him {idea}as one of his closest aides{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says that when they spoke, the king saw his ability, good conduct and manners, and told him: {reward}today you are with us, high in rank and fully trusted.{/reward}
now: The interview where you just told the truth, did not oversell, did not badmouth your old boss. The new manager says: I trust you. {idea}Years of quiet integrity can show up in a single conversation.{/idea}
old: Getting ahead depends on knowing the right people.
new: Character, kept in hard years, is what opens the door when it finally opens.
try: In one conversation today, just be plainly honest, with no spin.

title: Put me over the storehouses: I guard, and I know.
subtitle: Yusuf asks for the job he is suited for
then: Yusuf asked the king to put him in charge of the land's storehouses. Ibn Kathir says {idea}praising yourself is allowed when your ability is unknown and there is a need{/idea}. He described himself as an honest guard with knowledge of the work, so he could {reward}distribute the harvest wisely{/reward} in the drought.
now: The team needs someone to run the budget, and you know you can do it well. You stay quiet because speaking up feels like bragging. {idea}Saying I can do this, honestly, so people are served, is not arrogance.{/idea}
old: Mentioning my own strengths is always showing off.
new: Offering my real skills when people need them can be a way of serving.
try: Offer one skill you have to someone who needs it this week.

title: No good-doer's reward is ever lost.
subtitle: The slave and prisoner now moves freely in the land
then: Allah says He {reward}established Yusuf in the land{/reward}. Ibn Jarir said he now moved freely after prison, hardship and slavery. Ibn Kathir says Allah did not let {idea}his patience with his brothers and in prison{/idea} be lost, but rewarded it with help and victory.
now: The years you cared for a sick parent. The job where you stayed honest while others cut corners. The marriage you kept kind through hard seasons. {idea}None of it is lost.{/idea} {reward}Allah keeps the record.{/reward}
old: My patience went unnoticed, so it was for nothing.
new: Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
try: Remember one hard thing you were patient through, and thank Allah that He saw it.

title: Power in Egypt, but the Hereafter's reward is better.
subtitle: The bigger prize after the worldly one
then: Right after Yusuf's rise, Allah adds: {reward}the reward of the Hereafter is better{/reward} for those who believe and are mindful of Him. Ibn Kathir says what Allah prepared for Yusuf there is {idea}greater and more honored than the authority he had here{/idea}.
now: The promotion comes. The house is bought. The degree is framed. For a week you feel you have arrived. {idea}This verse says: good, and there is more.{/idea} The best part is not on this side.
old: Worldly success is the final proof that I made it.
new: Even the best success here is smaller than what Allah keeps for the mindful.
try: After your next small win, add one deed meant only for the Hereafter.

title: His brothers stood before him and did not know him.
subtitle: The drought brings them to Yusuf's court
then: The drought spread to Canaan, and Ya'qub sent his sons to Egypt for food. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf was {reward}a mercy to the people{/reward}, giving each family one camel-load. He knew his brothers at once. {trap}They never imagined the boy they sold would become a minister.{/trap}
now: Years later, the person who mocked you at school walks into your clinic, your shop, your office, needing help. They do not recognize you. {idea}How you treat them now is your test, not theirs.{/idea}
old: If I ever meet the people who hurt me, I will make them feel it.
new: When the tables turn, I get to choose to be a mercy.
try: Think of someone who once wronged you. Decide now how you would want to treat them.

title: Full measure, good hosting, and one request.
subtitle: Yusuf asks them to bring his brother

row.title: fair and generous
sub: even to those who hurt him

then: Yusuf {reward}honored his brothers and gave them all they needed{/reward}. As-Suddi reported that they had told him of a brother kept at home. Yusuf asked them to bring him, to show they had told the truth, and reminded them: {idea}I give full measure and I am the best of hosts.{/idea}
now: Your ex-colleague who took credit for your work now needs a reference. You could undersell them. {idea}Yusuf gave full measure to people who once sold him.{/idea} Fairness does not depend on whether they deserve it.
old: People who wronged me do not deserve my full fairness.
new: Full measure is my standard, whoever is standing in front of me.
try: Give someone you dislike exactly what is fair to them today, no less.

title: No brother next time, then no grain.
subtitle: A firm condition to bring the family together
then: After the kindness came a firm line. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf told them: if you come next time {trap}without your brother, you will get no grain{/trap} from me, nor come near me. He was {idea}encouraging them to return{/idea}, and to return with Binyamin.
now: A parent tells a teenager: you can have the car, but only if you are home by ten. A friend sets a boundary that keeps the relationship alive. {idea}Firmness can be a form of love with a purpose.{/idea}
old: Being kind means never setting conditions.
new: A firm condition can serve a good goal, even a reunion.
try: Set one clear, kind boundary today, and say why it matters.

title: We will work on our father, they promised.
subtitle: The same brothers, asking for a son again
then: The brothers promised Yusuf {idea}we will try our best with our father{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they wanted to prove they were truthful. But this was the father they had already {trap}asked once before for a son, and lost him{/trap}.
now: You promise your partner you will be home on time, again. You ask your parents for trust after you broke it last year. {idea}A promise lands on top of your history.{/idea} Rebuilding trust is slow work.
old: If I promise firmly enough, people should believe me.
new: My past actions decide how much my next promise weighs.
try: Keep one small promise today to someone whose trust you once let down.

title: He hid their payment back in their bags.
subtitle: A quiet gift to make them return
then: Yusuf told his servants to put the brothers' goods {reward}back into their saddlebags{/reward} without them knowing. Ibn Kathir notes it was said he did this because {idea}he feared they would have nothing left to trade{/idea} next time, so they could still come back.
now: You slip the money back into your mum's purse after she paid for dinner. You pay a struggling friend's bill without telling them. {reward}Quiet generosity that keeps the door open.{/reward}
old: If I help, they should know it was me.
new: The best help sometimes works best unseen.
try: Do one kind thing today that the person will never trace back to you.

title: Send our brother, we will guard him, they said again.
subtitle: The words Ya'qub had heard once before

row.title: years ago
sub: send Yusuf, we will guard him

row.title: today
sub: send Binyamin, we will guard him

then: Back home, the brothers told Ya'qub {trap}the grain is denied unless Binyamin comes{/trap}, and promised: we will guard him. Ibn Kathir points out these are {idea}the very words they used about Yusuf{/idea}: send him with us tomorrow, we will take care of him (12:12).
now: I'll drive carefully this time. I won't share your secret again. I'll pay you back by Friday. {trap}The exact words you said last time.{/trap} {idea}Same words need different actions to mean something.{/idea}
old: Saying it again with feeling should be enough.
new: When I repeat an old promise, only changed actions make it new.
try: Pick one promise you keep repeating. Do one concrete thing toward it today.

title: Allah is the best guardian, the Most Merciful.
subtitle: Ya'qub moves his trust from his sons to his Lord
then: Ya'qub asked: {trap}shall I trust you with him as I trusted you with his brother?{/trap} Then he turned to Allah. Ibn Kathir says he meant: Allah is the most merciful to me, in my old age and my longing, and {reward}I ask Him to return my son to me.{/reward}
now: Your child gets in the car with friends for the first time. Your teenager flies abroad. You cannot control the road. {idea}You can say: Allah is the best guardian, and mean it.{/idea}
old: I have to control everything to keep the people I love safe.
new: I do what I can, and leave the guarding to the One who guards best.
try: Next time someone you love leaves the house, say: Allah is the best guardian.

title: Our money came back, what more could we want?
subtitle: The returned goods become their argument
then: Opening their bags, the brothers found {reward}their goods returned{/reward}. Qatadah said they asked: what more can we want? Ibn Kathir says they used it {idea}to make their case more appealing{/idea}: food for the family, and an extra camel-load if Binyamin came.
now: A refund lands in your account. A colleague covers your shift. You immediately calculate what it means for you. {idea}Pause and ask who was kind, and why.{/idea}
old: Unexpected good just means a better deal for me.
new: Unexpected good is often someone's quiet care, and it is worth noticing.
try: Next time something unexpected and good comes your way, find out who to thank.

title: Swear by Allah, then I will send him.
subtitle: A father's oath and a father's trust
then: Ya'qub said he would not send Binyamin {idea}until they swore by Allah{/idea} to bring him back, unless they were all overwhelmed. When they swore, he said: {reward}Allah is Witness over what we say.{/reward} Ibn Ishaq said he had no choice, since they needed food to survive.
now: You sign the contract. You make the family agreement in the group chat. You shake on the deal. {idea}Remember who is also listening.{/idea} Allah witnesses every promise, yours included.
old: A promise is just between me and the other person.
new: Every promise I make is made in front of Allah.
try: Before you agree to something today, quietly remember that Allah is witness.

title: Enter by different gates, and trust in Allah.
subtitle: Taking precautions while knowing they are not the cause
then: Ya'qub told his sons to {idea}enter Egypt by different gates{/idea}. Ibn 'Abbas and others said he feared the evil eye for them. Yet he added: this cannot help you against Allah. {reward}The decision is only His; in Him I put my trust.{/reward}
now: You lock the door, check the tyres, set the reminder, back up the files. Then the worry still sits on your chest. {idea}Do the sensible thing, then hand the outcome to Allah.{/idea}
old: If I plan well enough, nothing can go wrong.
new: I take my precautions, and the result is still in Allah's hands.
try: After you take a precaution today, say: I put my trust in Allah, and let it go.
